beats.lead: Ask who invented the D-pad and most people say Gunpei Yokoi.
beats.note: Yokoi ran the division that shipped it. He isn't the name on the paperwork.

beats.name: Ichiro Shirai
beats.role: Nintendo's cross-shaped pad first shipped inside the Game & Watch version of Donkey Kong, credited on the eventual patent to Shirai rather than his better-known boss.

beats.lead: The patent itself came years after the product.
beats.text: Nintendo filed for it in August 1985 and wasn't granted it until August 1987.
beats.note: Five years after the D-pad had already shipped to shops.

beats.name: William F. Palisek
beats.role: Filed the actual first cross-style four-way controller patent, for Tiger Electronics — it shipped on Tiger's 1980 football handheld as the 'Playmaker' button, two years before Nintendo's version existed.

beats.lead: So what did Nintendo's patent actually claim?
beats.text: Not the cross shape — a smaller pad, built for the left thumb, using membrane switches instead of Palisek's bulkier domed ones.
beats.note: That's the whole distinguishing claim, in writing.

beats.line: The most recognisable button on any controller, credited to the wrong household name.
